concepts.learning_objective: Identify the biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem and distinguish natural from human-made ecosystems.
Explain the roles of producers, consumers and decomposers and how they depend on one another.

topics.title: Food chains, trophic levels and food webs

concepts.learning_objective: Place organisms of a food chain at the correct trophic level and consumer category.
Explain why feeding relationships form branching food webs rather than single straight chains.

topics.title: Flow of energy in an ecosystem

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the 10 percent rule to calculate energy available at successive trophic levels.
Explain why energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional and diminishes at each level.
Explain how non-degradable chemicals accumulate progressively along a food chain.
Describe how pesticides from fields enter food chains through soil and water.
Describe how ozone forms in the upper atmosphere and how it shields the Earth from UV radiation.
Relate the drop in ozone to CFCs and evaluate steps taken to limit the damage.
Classify substances as biodegradable or non-biodegradable and explain the role of enzyme specificity.
Evaluate everyday practices and choices for reducing and disposing of waste.
